title: The Water Line
blurb: Una botella y una línea azul.
summary: Nina y Bruno descansan y toman agua en el parque.
text: Nina has a clear bottle. There is a blue line on it. She puts water in the bottle. The water is at the line. She puts the bottle in her bag. At the park, she drinks some water. Now the water is below the line. Bruno has his own bowl. Nina puts water in his bowl too. They sit under a tree. Before they go home, Nina closes her bottle and puts it back in her bag.

comprehension_questions.question: Where is the water at first?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Al llenar la botella, el agua llega a la línea azul.

comprehension_questions.question: What does Nina do before going home?
options: She leaves the bottle under the tree
comprehension_questions.explanation: Antes de irse cierra la botella y la guarda.

title: The Curtain in the Afternoon
blurb: Una cortina cambia la luz de una habitación.
summary: Nina encuentra una solución sencilla para leer con comodidad.
text: Nina bought a yellow curtain for her living room. In the shop, the colour looked warm and bright. At home, she hung it beside the window. The next afternoon, sunlight came through the cloth and made the white wall look yellow. Nina liked the colour, but she could not read comfortably in her usual chair because the light was too strong. She moved the chair away from the window and tried again. This time she could read, and the room still looked cheerful. She did not need to return the curtain. On the receipt, she wrote the size of the window. She wanted to remember it when she bought a second curtain for the other room.

comprehension_questions.question: What changed the appearance of the wall?
comprehension_questions.explanation: La luz atravesó la tela amarilla y cambió el aspecto de la pared blanca.

comprehension_questions.question: How did Nina solve her reading problem?
comprehension_questions.explanation: Movió la silla para evitar la luz demasiado intensa.

comprehension_questions.question: Why did she write on the receipt?
options: To record the price of a chair
comprehension_questions.explanation: Anotó las medidas para recordarlas al comprar otra cortina.

title: The Tunnel under the Compost
blurb: Observar un jardín requiere revisar el método.
summary: Un grupo escolar aprende a interpretar un registro incompleto.
text:
When a school garden opened its compost bin, the children found a narrow tunnel near the bottom. One group wanted to cover it immediately. Another wanted to put food beside it to see what would appear. Their teacher suggested observing without touching or feeding anything first.

Nina helped them place a camera outside the bin, pointing towards the opening. The first night produced no useful pictures because a leaf moved in front of the lens. They moved the camera slightly and secured the leaf away from it. The following morning, the recording showed a small animal entering the tunnel after dark.

The teacher sent the recording to the garden coordinator, who arranged advice about managing the compost and keeping the area suitable for school activities. The children had not needed to catch the animal to learn something useful. They also discovered that an empty recording did not necessarily mean nothing had happened. Sometimes it meant their way of looking needed an adjustment.

comprehension_questions.question: Why was the first recording unhelpful?
options: The camera was inside a classroom
comprehension_questions.explanation: Una hoja se movió delante del lente; el resultado no demostraba ausencia de actividad.

comprehension_questions.question: What did they do with the useful recording?
options: They used it to choose food for the animal
They posted the animal's exact location
They shared it with the coordinator
comprehension_questions.explanation: La docente envió la grabación a la persona encargada para organizar asesoramiento.

comprehension_questions.question: What did they learn about observation?
options: The method can explain missing evidence
Catching an animal is always necessary
One empty recording proves a place is unused
comprehension_questions.explanation: La falta de imágenes podía deberse al método de observación y no a falta de actividad.

title: The Subtitle That Arrived Too Soon
blurb: El momento de un subtítulo cambia lo que entendemos.
summary: Un club de cine ajusta subtítulos según la atención del público.
text:
A film club asked volunteers to subtitle a short comedy. The dialogue was easy to understand, but Nina noticed that one translated line appeared several seconds before the character spoke. It revealed the answer to a question that the scene deliberately left hanging. The translation was accurate; the timing changed the joke.

The editor proposed displaying longer blocks of text so viewers would have more time to read. That could help with reading speed, yet it might reveal even more of the exchange before the actors delivered it. Nina suggested splitting the line at a natural pause, then testing the sequence with viewers who had not seen the film.

During the test, two viewers missed a short line while looking at an important visual detail. The volunteers adjusted both its duration and its position relative to the action. They kept the meaning, but treated attention as a limited resource rather than assuming that viewers could watch and read everything simultaneously.

The finished subtitles were not simply a transcript in another language. Their success depended on when information became available, and on what else the audience was being asked to notice.

comprehension_questions.question: What spoiled the joke initially?
options: An incorrect translation of the answer
A subtitle disclosed information too early
comprehension_questions.explanation: El contenido era correcto, pero revelaba la respuesta antes del momento previsto.

comprehension_questions.question: Why might longer blocks be a poor solution?
options: They could disclose more dialogue prematurely
They prevent any reading time adjustment
comprehension_questions.explanation: Dar más tiempo con bloques largos podía anticipar todavía más información.

comprehension_questions.question: What does the viewer test demonstrate?
options: Timing must account for competing visual attention
comprehension_questions.explanation: Los espectadores también necesitaban mirar una acción importante; lectura e imagen compiten por atención.

title: The Reference Sample in the Freezer
blurb: Una referencia aprobada también puede cambiar.
summary: Un laboratorio distingue continuidad documental de estabilidad material.
text:
A small food laboratory was comparing the colour of new batches against a reference sample kept in a freezer. The sample had served for months, and its label carried an impressive sequence of approval signatures. When a technician proposed replacing it, colleagues worried that a new reference would disrupt comparisons with earlier results.

Nina, reviewing the laboratory's documentation workflow, asked what evidence showed that the reference itself had remained stable. The records demonstrated that staff had checked new batches against it; they did not demonstrate that freezing had preserved its original colour indefinitely. Repeated agreement with the same comparator could therefore conceal a shared drift.

The laboratory did not discard its historical records. Instead, its technical lead arranged an independent check using the laboratory's established procedures and documented the link between the old reference and its replacement. Earlier observations remained intelligible, while future ones no longer relied solely on the assumption that an approved object could not change.

The awkward point was institutional as much as technical. Each signature certified an action performed at a particular time, yet the accumulated signatures had come to look like a permanent property of the sample. Continuity required preserving the relationship between measurements, not preserving one physical object at any cost. What appeared to threaten comparability was also an opportunity to establish what comparability had actually rested on.

comprehension_questions.question: What gap did Nina identify?
options: No one had compared the new batches
Checks against the reference did not establish the reference's stability
comprehension_questions.explanation: Usar repetidamente la misma referencia no demuestra que ella misma se conserve estable.

comprehension_questions.question: Why document the link between references?
options: To maintain interpretable continuity across the change
comprehension_questions.explanation: Relacionar ambas referencias permite interpretar resultados anteriores y futuros sin borrar la historia.

comprehension_questions.question: What is the institutional misconception?
options: Approval can come to be treated as an enduring material property
Every signature guarantees a separate measurement
Historical documentation must be discarded when an object changes
comprehension_questions.explanation: Las firmas acreditaban acciones en momentos concretos, pero se interpretaban como una cualidad permanente de la muestra.

title: The Joke No One Would Translate Twice
blurb: Un silencio elegido transforma una historia compartida.
summary: Dos versiones de una broma revelan distintas relaciones con el público.
text:
An oral-history archive held two recordings of a family joke, told decades apart. In the earlier version, the teller imitated a neighbour's elaborate manner of speaking. In the later one, her daughter retained the same incident but omitted the imitation. Asked to translate both recordings for an exhibition, a translator initially treated the difference as a loss: the daughter's account seemed to preserve the facts while flattening the performance.

During a consultation, however, the daughter explained that the imitation had become uncomfortable after the neighbour's grandchildren joined the family's social circle. She still found the incident funny; she no longer wished to invite laughter at a voice. What the translator had construed as diminished expressiveness was also an adjustment in whom the telling positioned as a permissible object of amusement.

A literal restoration of the missing imitation would thus have supplied something the later teller had chosen to withhold. Conversely, presenting only the daughter's explanation risked making the earlier performance stand for a settled moral position that its teller had never been asked to articulate. The archive possessed two acts of telling, not a controlled experiment in changing attitudes.

The exhibition retained both recordings and commissioned separate translations, accompanied by a short account of the consultation. Neither version was promoted as the authentic joke from which the other had deviated. Their relationship lay partly in what persisted and partly in what had become unsayable in a particular company. Translation here required fidelity not only to the words that travelled, but to the social work performed by their conspicuous absence.

comprehension_questions.question: What revises the translator's initial interpretation?
options: The daughter reveals that the incident never happened
The omission reflects a changed social relationship
The archive proves the imitation was mistranscribed
comprehension_questions.explanation: La hija relaciona la omisión con nuevas relaciones sociales, no con una pérdida de capacidad expresiva.

comprehension_questions.question: Why avoid treating the recordings as a controlled experiment?
options: Their tellers were responding to distinct occasions and relationships
comprehension_questions.explanation: Son actos situados de narración; no aíslan variables ni prueban una evolución moral única.

comprehension_questions.question: What does fidelity require in the final paragraph?
options: Selecting the earlier version as the original
Recognising the function of deliberate omission
comprehension_questions.explanation: La fidelidad incluye entender qué hace socialmente el silencio elegido, además de traducir lo expresado.
